purpose: Empirical gateway/chokepoint seed layer for the World Map. Coordinates are approximate visualization anchors, not navigation data. Transit observations are dated rather than treated as timeless capacity.
source_note: Oil-transit observations use the U.S. Energy Information Administration Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026 energy-security chokepoint table for Q2 2026. EIA states that its analysis uses Vortexa tanker tracking and Panama Canal Authority data with EIA calculations.

malacca-strait.label: Strait of Malacca
malacca-strait.coordinate_note: Approximate map anchor for visualization only; not suitable for navigation.

observation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration — Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026

malacca-strait.description: Major maritime chokepoint linking the Indian and Pacific Oceans and a critical route for energy flows into East and Southeast Asia.

hormuz-strait.label: Strait of Hormuz
hormuz-strait.coordinate_note: Approximate map anchor for visualization only; not suitable for navigation.

observation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration — Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026

hormuz-strait.description: Strategic passage between the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman; alternatives can move only part of the normal oil flow when disruption occurs.

suez-sumed.label: Suez Canal / SUMED corridor
suez-sumed.coordinate_note: Approximate map anchor for visualization only; not suitable for navigation.

observation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration — Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026

alternatives.note: Traffic can reroute around southern Africa when Red Sea/Suez access is disrupted; this does not imply equal distance, cost or capacity.
alternatives.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration — Short-Term Energy Outlook, August 2026

suez-sumed.description: Egyptian canal-and-pipeline corridor connecting Red Sea and Mediterranean energy and shipping flows.

bab-el-mandeb.description: Narrow passage connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea; disruptions alter Europe–Asia routing and can divert traffic around southern Africa.

panama-canal.description: Interoceanic canal linking Atlantic and Pacific shipping; water availability and operating constraints can materially affect transit patterns.
